subject: Post-call: DPA clarifications & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@acme-payments.com>, Jared Mills <jared.mills@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: DPA clarifications & next steps

Hi Alice / Jared —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to meet the Acme Payments team. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the DPA/privacy items we discussed: 

1) Roles: Per our standard DPA, Redwood acts as a processor on behalf of Acme (controller) for customer-provided data sent to the API. We are happy to confirm this in writing and add specific language if your legal team prefers explicit controller/processor clauses.

2) Data residency: Hosted Redwood endpoints are available in multiple regions. Default production data processing for your account would be in the US, but we can route and store logs/responses to EU regions if you need EU residency.

3) PII & embeddings: We do not use customer content to train models. Embeddings and generated outputs are treated as processed data; customers can opt-in to have indexing/long-term storage disabled.

4) Retention & logging: Our default policy for request payload retention is 30 days; system logs and audit trails are retained for 90 days unless otherwise agreed. We can offer custom retention windows for enterprise contracts.

5) Subprocessors: We'll provide a current list of subprocessors (CDN, cloud infra, monitoring). We maintain a subprocessors list and notify customers of changes per the DPA.

6) Breach notice: Standard DPA includes a 72-hour notification window for incidents that materially affect customer data; we can add escalation contacts and an SLA for acknowledgement.

Attachments: I've attached our current DPA with marked-up items (dpa_redlines_acme_v2.pdf) and a short security disclosures spreadsheet.

Next steps: 
- Please confirm the items above and any specific redlines your legal team needs.
- If helpful, I can loop in Privacy (cc’ing Ben) to handle legal redlines and subprocessors list.
- If you confirm EU residency is required, we’ll open a ticket with infra to scope the region routing work.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: DPA clarifications & next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few follow-ups from our side: 

- Can you confirm whether Redwood considers telemetry/usage metrics as "personal data" when tied to user IDs? If so, do you treat that telemetry under processor terms or is there any joint-controller exposure?

- For embeddings: we need assurance that raw PII will never be persistently stored in embeddings or reused. Do you have a technical control we can point our engineers to?

- Retention: 30 days default sounds reasonable, but our retention policy requires that customer content be deletable on demand. Can Redwood provide an on-demand purge API or confirm manual deletion procedure and SLAs?

- Subprocessors: please send the list and the process for notification of changes. Our legal team will review the redlines in the attached DPA.

Looping in our legal team (cc) to coordinate redlines.

Best,
Jared
Senior Product Manager, Acme Payments

- Reiterate that Redwood is a processor and provide the exact DPA clause (I attached the excerpt).
- Confirm telemetry is treated as customer data; we can classify identifiable telemetry as PII if it's provided by the customer; generally treated under processor obligations.

- Offer the on-demand purge API (we have an existing endpoint customers can use; suggest offering 72-hour SLA for purge confirmation for enterprise deals).

If legal pushes on controller vs joint controller for certain telemetry cases, we should propose a scoped joint-processing clause only where both parties decide to co-determine purposes (rare).

Hi Jared / Alice / Acme Legal —

Thanks for the detailed questions. Quick answers and artifacts attached below to help your review team.

1) Controller / Processor: Redwood operates as a processor under the DPA for customer-provided inputs. Where telemetry or integrations require co-determination of purposes we can negotiate a limited joint-processing clause, but by default Redwood is the processor.

2) Telemetry & PII: Telemetry tied to customer identifiers is treated as customer data under processor obligations. We can mark telemetry that includes user identifiers as deletable and scoped to the customer's retention policy.

3) Embeddings / reuse: Redwood does not use customer content to train models or to improve base model weights. Embeddings derived from customer content are ephemeral by default; we can disable persistent indexing for your account.

4) On-demand purge: We offer an on-demand purge API for enterprise customers (example in attached doc). For this deal we can commit to a 72-hour purge confirmation SLA once a purge request is submitted and authenticated.

5) Retention windows: Default 30 days for request payloads; 90 days for system logs/audit trails. Custom retention windows are available in contract.

6) Subprocessors & notifications: Current subprocessors list and contacts here: https://www.redwood.com/subprocessors (snapshot attached in "security_disclosures.xlsx"). We notify customers 30 days in advance of substantive changes as per the DPA.

7) Breach notice: Redwood’s standard DPA includes a 72-hour notification for material incidents affecting customer data, with a documented escalation path. We are open to adding a named point of contact and SLA for acknowledgement.

Attached: dpa_redlines_acme_v2.pdf (with our comments), security_disclosures.xlsx (subprocessors snapshot), purge_api_example.txt

Next steps: 
- Please have your legal team review the attached redlines. If they accept, we'll finalize and send a DocuSign envelope for execution: https://www.docusign.com/ACME-DPA-Envelope-98765
- If you need privacy to sign off on any modified controller/joint-processing language, we can loop Privacy in.

Happy to jump on a short call with legal if that helps move the redlines faster.

Best,
